skill.name: deploying-postgres-k8s
skill.description: Guides PostgreSQL deployment on Kubernetes with CloudNativePG, including operator installation, high availability, secrets, backups, monitoring, troubleshooting, and cleanup.
skill.summary: Deploy and operate CloudNativePG PostgreSQL clusters on Kubernetes.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks; the verifier performs local structure checks only. Confirmed risks include remote manifest installation, plaintext database credentials, terminal secret disclosure, and destructive PVC deletion. No prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Use Kubernetes secretKeyRef values and placeholder secret names. Remove literal passwords from manifests, migration commands, and connection examples.

remediation.issue: Installation and cleanup trust remote manifests without integrity checks.
remediation.suggestion: Pin immutable artifact digests or verified checksums. Pin Helm chart versions and review downloaded manifests before applying or deleting resources.

remediation.issue: Credential retrieval commands print secret URIs.
remediation.suggestion: Reference secrets directly from workloads. For diagnostics, warn users about terminal logs and show redacted output practices.

remediation.issue: Cleanup can delete all database persistent volumes.
remediation.suggestion: Require backup verification, explicit confirmation, namespace selection, and Kubernetes context checks before presenting the PVC deletion command.

content.user_title: Deploy PostgreSQL on Kubernetes with CloudNativePG
content.value_statement: Operating PostgreSQL directly on Kubernetes requires careful availability, storage, secret, and backup configuration. This skill provides practical CloudNativePG deployment and operations guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains CloudNativePG installation using a direct manifest or Helm.
Provides development and three-instance production cluster configurations.
Shows bootstrap database, application secret, and service endpoint configuration.
Documents PostgreSQL access, database creation, migrations, and connectivity checks.
Provides S3 backup, scheduled backup, Prometheus monitoring, and log guidance.
Covers readiness checks, common failures, and cluster cleanup commands.
limitations: It does not provision a Kubernetes cluster, storage class, object store, or monitoring stack.
Example resource values require workload testing before production use.
It does not cover managed PostgreSQL services or standalone Docker deployments.
Some credential examples require security hardening before use.

use_cases.title: Create a local development database
use_cases.description: Build a single-instance CloudNativePG cluster with basic storage and readiness checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare a production PostgreSQL cluster
use_cases.description: Define three instances, resource limits, anti-affinity, monitoring, and application connectivity.

use_cases.title: Operate backups and incidents
use_cases.description: Configure S3 backups, inspect logs, test connectivity, and diagnose readiness failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a development cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a single-instance CloudNativePG cluster in {namespace} using {storage_class} and {storage_size}. Include installation and readiness checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a three-instance PostgreSQL cluster for {workload}. Include resources, storage, anti-affinity, secrets, services, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add backup and monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my CloudNativePG cluster with {object_store} backups, retention, scheduled backups, PodMonitor metrics, and restore validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a deployment plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these CloudNativePG requirements: {requirements}. Identify availability, security, storage, backup, migration, observability, and recovery gaps with prioritized changes.

output_examples.input: Create a production cluster with three instances and 100Gi storage.
output: A three-instance CloudNativePG cluster plan with persistent storage and pod anti-affinity.
Resource requests, limits, monitoring settings, readiness checks, and application service guidance.

output_examples.input: Add daily S3 backups with a 30-day retention period.
output: A backup configuration referencing Kubernetes-managed object store credentials.
A daily scheduled backup, retention policy, status checks, and restore validation checklist.

output_examples.input: Diagnose a cluster that never becomes ready.
output_examples.output: A focused sequence for checking cluster conditions, pods, storage claims, operator status, events, and PostgreSQL logs.

best_practices: Pin operator and chart versions, verify artifacts, and review manifests before cluster changes.
Store credentials in Kubernetes secrets and avoid printing connection URIs.
Test backups, restores, failover, storage capacity, and resource limits before production launch.
anti_patterns: Do not embed database passwords in manifests, shell history, or migration commands.
Do not delete persistent volume claims before confirming backups, namespace, and Kubernetes context.
Do not use example resource settings without workload measurements and storage validation.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Kubernetes cluster?
faq.answer: No. It assumes a working Kubernetes cluster, kubectl access, and a suitable storage class.

faq.question: Which PostgreSQL operator does it use?
faq.answer: It uses CloudNativePG and documents direct manifest and Helm installation paths.

faq.question: Can I use it for local development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a single-instance development configuration with smaller storage and resource expectations.

faq.question: Does it configure high availability?
faq.answer: Yes. The production example uses three instances, automatic failover, and pod anti-affinity.

faq.question: Does it support backups?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers S3-compatible object storage, retention, scheduled backups, and related credential references.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready without changes?
faq.answer: No. Validate storage, resources, credentials, network controls, backup recovery, and operator versions for your environment.
